answer:
The simulation uses OpenFOAM's interFoam solver in transient mode to model gravity-driven sloshing of water in a closed rectangular tank.
The tank geometry is a rectangular box with dimensions 1.0 m in x, 0.6 m in y, and 0.1 m in z.
Gravity is set to g = (0 -9.81 0), acting in the negative y direction.
Two configurations are specified: a 2D validation case and a 3D final case. All parameters are identical between the two except where explicitly noted.
The 2D validation configuration uses a blockMesh grid of 200 x 120 x 1 cells, with the frontAndBack boundary patches set to type empty.
The 3D final configuration uses a blockMesh grid of 200 x 120 x 20 cells, with the frontAndBack boundary patches set to wall type (noSlip for U, fixedFluxPressure for p_rgh, zeroGradient for alpha.water).
The remaining four boundary patches (bottom at y=0, top at y=0.6, left at x=0, right at x=1.0) are wall type in both configurations, using noSlip for U, fixedFluxPressure for p_rgh, and zeroGradient for alpha.water.
The initial velocity field is U = (0 0 0) everywhere, and the initial p_rgh is 0 everywhere.
The initial free surface is imposed as a staircase approximation of a tilted plane, built with ten boxToCell entries in setFieldsDict. The default field value is alpha.water = 0 (air). Each box overrides alpha.water to 1 within its region.
The ten boxes are each 0.1 m wide in x and span the full z extent (0 to 0.1 m). Their y-extents (water heights) are: 0.255 m, 0.265 m, 0.275 m, 0.285 m, 0.295 m, 0.305 m, 0.315 m, 0.325 m, 0.335 m, 0.345 m, assigned to x-ranges 0-0.1, 0.1-0.2, 0.2-0.3, 0.3-0.4, 0.4-0.5, 0.5-0.6, 0.6-0.7, 0.7-0.8, 0.8-0.9, 0.9-1.0 respectively.
The water phase properties are: rho = 1000 kg/m3, nu = 1e-6 m2/s.
The air phase properties are: rho = 1.2 kg/m3, nu = 1.5e-5 m2/s.
The surface tension coefficient for the water-air interface is sigma = 0.072 N/m.
Time control parameters are: endTime = 10 s, deltaT = 1e-3 s, maxCo = 0.5, writeInterval = 0.05 s.
The 2D validation case is intended to verify the sloshing oscillation period and amplitude decay of the tilted free surface settling under gravity before proceeding to the 3D run.
The 3D case is the final deliverable, targeting a full three-dimensional sloshing solution.
No tank acceleration, inlet velocity, or external impulse is applied at any time; the sole driving mechanism is gravity acting on the initially tilted free surface.
